blocks.markdown:
We are positioning the first public article for **AI coding power users**: people already using Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor-style agents, or similar harnesses and feeling artifact sprawl.

The article should start as a **personal origin story**, not a generic launch announcement: agents got better at building things, but the human-facing artifacts were scattered across chat, Markdown dumps, and loose HTML files. harness-deck became the local pane of glass where agents can show human-facing work.
blocks.title: Decisions already made

blocks.html:
Thesis: AI coding agents need a shared presentation layer. Chat is the conversation; harness-deck is where agents put the artifacts they want a human to inspect.

Before

Claude writes a Markdown report. Codex drops an HTML mockup. OpenCode leaves a decision in scrollback. Everything is technically visible, but nothing is centered.

chat transcriptloose HTMLlost decision

Contract

Every harness emits the same small report manifest: prose, metrics, comparisons, raw HTML mockups, and interactive questions.

report.jsontyped blockshtml canvas

Pane of glass

harness-deck renders reports into one local dashboard, grouped by project, with asks and approvals that survive context clears.

dashboardinboxresponses.json

Public story

The Medium article explains the workflow gap first, then shows harness-deck as a concrete local-first solution.

items.text: Starts with a concrete pain: scattered Markdown, HTML mockups, and decisions disappearing into chat.

Broader and more reusable: every AI harness needs a shared pane of glass.
Risks sounding abstract before readers feel the actual problem.
Could bury the best story: the tool came from real artifact sprawl.
